synopsis: UTAC submitted virtual-testing proposals to the United Nations working group on automatic emergency braking; the detailed evidence supplied here concerns on-road AEBS rather than heavy off-road machines [f16110, f7846]. Its earlier AEBS-12-07 proposal allowed virtual validation within a validity domain and proposed removing 10% of the 10 repeated automotive AEBS runs per scenario [f7860, f7845, f7846]. The later UTAC CERAM document AEBS-16-03 includes a 30% physical-test figure alongside validation using 11 SUT-and-target variables and three metrics: IAPE, Double th, and interval [f7686]. Although one account describes that figure as a minimum, the corpus explicitly says it cannot be reconciled with adopted UN R152 text, which leaves physical confirmatory-test numbers to manufacturer–authority agreement; the adopted text governs [f7547, f8188]. UTAC's curve-comparison approach combines peak time, peak value, curve shape and error, but the supplied facts do not establish its applicability to off-road machines [f7771, f7846].
